summary: A median age of 19.5 and a 92% concentration in the 18–34 bracket tells you almost everything: this 1.7-square-mile census area is essentially the on-campus and immediately adjacent housing footprint of UC Davis itself, not the broader city of Davis. That $17,625 median household income and 67.7% poverty rate reflect a population overwhelmingly composed of students whose reported earnings don't capture parental support, financial aid, or future earning power — so those figures describe a statistical artifact more than material deprivation. The flat Sacramento Valley terrain here is almost comically bikeable, and UC Davis has one of the highest rates of bicycle commuting of any university in the country, with an extensive network of bike paths threading through campus and into the surrounding town. Summers are serious — average highs around 76°F annually means July and August routinely push past 100°F — while winters are mild and foggy. With 60.8% holding a bachelor's degree or higher (many mid-completion), the area functions as a knowledge-economy pipeline; the university and UC Davis Medical Center in Sacramento are the dominant employers. Median rent at $1,560 against that nominal income yields a price-to-income ratio that looks alarming on paper but operates within the logic of a campus housing market, not a traditional residential one. This is a place defined entirely by the rhythm of an academic calendar — not a city in any conventional sense.
